title: Lina and the Wiggly Banners
markdown:
In Sunny Meadow the colourful banners were going up for the Berry Blossom Festival. They looked all wrong. One drooped. Another had stripes that stretched too long on one side.

Lina frowned. “They don’t look right.” She tried to fix one; it grew more crooked. Moss the hedgehog scurried closer. “Wiggly and wonky,” he whispered.

Auntie June sat down with a warm smile. She folded a piece of paper in half and showed Lina. “One side matches the other exactly.”

A light flickered. “That’s it. They need to match.”

They gathered the fabric. Lina folded it in half, sides lying perfectly on each other. “Same shape and size — balanced. Like a mirror.”

They folded and pinned. When they unfurled the new banners, they gasped. The colours flowed in an even line, each side a reflection. Sunny Meadow looked ready, bright and balanced.

June beamed and named it once: symmetrical. Both sides the same, a perfect reflection — butterfly wings, if you needed a picture. She did not send Lina hunting delightful secrets.

Lina said the word back, pleased at how simple it was. She looked at the meadow and left the next banner on the table, already folded, so the last pole would not go wiggly after the others had learned to behave.
